name: Quote Request Assistant
value_proposition: Paste a quote request, extract labelled scope against the owner's written qualification rules, and get a draft acknowledgment — the owner prices and sends.
persona: A contractor, home-service business, agency, or custom shop getting about 5-30 quote requests a week.
problem: Quote requests arrive in inconsistent formats. Staff reconstruct scope from messy form and email text before anyone can price the job.
workflow: 1. The person writes qualification rules before any request is judged: service area, minimum project size, services offered, work that is out of scope, and internal notes that must never appear in a customer draft. PERSON DECIDES: what a good-fit request is, and which phrases are internal only.

2. The person copies one quote request from a form or email into plain text. They remove payment details, account passwords, and any columns the workflow does not need. This is a pasted request, not a live inbox or form connector. PERSON DECIDES: which request to review and what to leave out.

3. The person checks the data settings of their AI assistant (chat history, training use, and file retention) before pasting anything. File upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings. PERSON DECIDES: whether to paste the request as text, upload a file, or not use AI for this request at all.
4. The person pastes the Scope Extraction Prompt, their rules from the Qualification Rules Worksheet, the service catalog, and the request text.

5. AI extracts only what the request stated. It labels CONFIRMED facts (work type, size, location, stated timeline, named material, requester) separately from AI INTERPRETATION (budget sensitivity, unknown structure condition, whether a date is a preference). It does not invent square footage, budget, addresses, or dates. Approximate wording such as 'maybe 300 sq ft' stays approximate.

6. AI applies the written qualification rules before any FIT label. FIT YES only when location is in the service area, size meets the minimum, and the work type is offered. FIT NO when the work is out of scope or the location is outside the service area, with the matching rule shown. If location, size, or work type is missing, or the work is close to the catalog but not listed, AI writes NEEDS YOUR CHECK and does not mark FIT NO. PERSON DECIDES: whether an unusual request is still worth a quote.

7. AI lists clarifying questions and writes a draft acknowledgment that contains no price, cost band, markup, or supplier name. The draft is not sent. AI also fills a suggested tracker row. PERSON DECIDES: which questions to ask, whether the draft is sent, what price to give, and whether the tracker row is added.

8. The person uses the Reply Review Checklist before contacting the requester. PERSON DECIDES: whether to ask questions, price the job, decline, or do nothing. The person prices and sends in their own mail or CRM. The Blueprint never sends, edits, cancels, or pays.
before: Requests sit in an inbox until someone has time to read them carefully, and some are lost.
after: Every pasted request has a structured scope, a fit judgment with reasons, and a draft reply the owner reviews before pricing or sending.

guided_demo.summary: A public, six-step walkthrough at /blueprints/quote-request-assistant using one fictional website-form request from Jordan Hale, dated 2026-05-12, for a back deck in Riverside. The owner's written rules are service area Riverside, minimum 150 sq ft, offered deck replacement and railings, and roofing out of scope. The demo extracts CONFIRMED facts from the request, labels budget sensitivity as AI INTERPRETATION, shows FIT YES with the matching rules, checks three facts against the request, shows two clarifying questions and a draft that is not sent, and ends with a tracker row the owner would add. Confirmed facts, AI interpretation, and recommended actions are labelled with text, not color alone. Every name, size, and date is invented. No live form, inbox, or CRM is attached.
steps: Step 1 of 6 - The request and the rules: show the fictional website-form request from Jordan Hale received 2026-05-12 with the exact text 'Need our back deck redone, maybe 300 sq ft, composite if not crazy expensive. Hoping before July. We're in Riverside.' Show the qualification rules table with service_area Riverside, minimum_size_sq_ft 150, offered 'deck replacement (wood or composite); railings', out_of_scope 'roofing; new-home construction', and never_in_draft 'prices; cost bands; markups; supplier names'. Label the request invented. State that no live form, inbox, or CRM is attached.

Step 2 of 6 - Extract with labels: show CONFIRMED lines containing 'deck replacement', 'maybe 300 sq ft', 'Riverside', 'hoping before July', 'composite', and 'Jordan Hale'. Show AI INTERPRETATION text containing 'if not crazy expensive' and 'requested window, not a booked start date'. Show the text labels 'CONFIRMED', 'AI INTERPRETATION', and 'RECOMMENDED ACTION' as visible words, not as color or icon alone. Do not show a price.

Step 3 of 6 - Fit against written rules: show the exact heading 'FIT: YES'. Show reasons containing 'Riverside', '150', and 'deck replacement'. Show the sentence 'A roofing request in Mesa would be FIT NO (out of catalog; outside service area).' Show the sentence 'A curved custom deck in Riverside that is not listed as a catalog item would be NEEDS YOUR CHECK, not FIT NO.'

Step 4 of 6 - Check the facts: show the CONFIRMED line with location = Riverside. A 'Check facts against the request' button shows three rows (location Riverside vs Riverside, size maybe 300 sq ft vs maybe 300 sq ft, work_type deck replacement vs back deck redone), each labelled with the text 'Matches'.

Step 5 of 6 - Questions and draft: show exactly two questions containing 'condition of the existing deck' and 'railing replacement'. Show a draft acknowledgment that contains 'Jordan', 'Riverside', '300 sq ft', and 'before July', and that does not contain a dollar amount, a cost band, a markup, or a supplier name. Show the exact sentence 'Do not send this draft.'

Step 6 of 6 - You price and send: show a tracker table with columns request_id, received, requester, location, work_type, size_sq_ft, material, timeline, fit, open_questions, status and one data row QR-1001, 2026-05-12, Jordan Hale, Riverside, deck replacement, 300, composite, before July, YES, existing structure; railing included, needs pricing. State the exact sentences 'You price it. You send it. The kit changes nothing.' and 'Do not send this draft.' Explain that the person adds the tracker row, prices the job, and sends any reply themselves. Offer a link to the Premium kit labelled as private preview with sign-in required.

guided_demo.sample_output:
CONFIRMED: work_type = deck replacement. size = maybe 300 sq ft. location = Riverside. timeline stated = hoping before July. material mentioned = composite. requester = Jordan Hale. received = 2026-05-12. source = website form.
AI INTERPRETATION: budget-sensitive because of "if not crazy expensive". "before July" is a requested window, not a booked start date. Existing structure condition is unknown.
FIT: YES. Riverside is in service_area. 300 is above minimum_size_sq_ft 150. deck replacement is offered.
NEEDS YOUR CHECK: existing structure condition; whether railing is included.
Questions: What is the condition of the existing deck? Should the quote include railing replacement?
DRAFT ACKNOWLEDGMENT (not sent): Thank you, Jordan. We received your request for a back deck replacement in Riverside, about 300 sq ft, with composite as a preference, and a hope to finish before July. We will review the scope and follow up with questions before we price anything.
TRACKER: QR-1001 | 2026-05-12 | Jordan Hale | Riverside | deck replacement | 300 | composite | before July | YES | existing structure; railing included | needs pricing
RECOMMENDED ACTION (you decide): Add the tracker row. Ask the two questions or price the job. You price it. You send it. The kit changes nothing.

kit_contents.title: Quote Request Setup Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Step-by-step setup for one review. It covers writing qualification rules (service area, minimum size, services offered, out-of-scope work, never-in-draft notes), copying one form or email request as plain text, removing payment details and other columns the workflow does not need, checking the AI tool's data settings before pasting, and the rule that this is a pasted request, not a live connector. It notes that file upload support differs by ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini plan, account, and admin settings, and that the request can be pasted as text instead.

kit_contents.title: Scope Extraction Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that extracts only stated fields, keeps approximate wording such as 'maybe 300 sq ft', labels CONFIRMED, AI INTERPRETATION, and RECOMMENDED ACTION separately, and forbids invented sizes, budgets, addresses, dates, prices, sending, and adding a tracker row.

kit_contents.title: Fit Review Prompt
kit_contents.purpose: Copyable prompt that applies the owner's written qualification rules before any FIT label, outputs FIT YES, FIT NO, or NEEDS YOUR CHECK with the matching rule, refuses to auto-reject an unusual request that is close to the catalog, and forbids sending, pricing, leaking internal notes, and editing a CRM.

kit_contents.title: Qualification Rules Worksheet
kit_contents.purpose: Browser-only form where the person writes service area, minimum project size, services offered, out-of-scope work, and internal notes that must never appear in a draft. It generates a copyable rules block to paste with the prompts. Nothing is saved to Atlas.

kit_contents.title: Quote Tracker Template
kit_contents.purpose: Column layout (request_id, received, requester, location, work_type, size_sq_ft, material, timeline, fit, open_questions, status) with allowed fit values YES, NO, NEEDS YOUR CHECK, allowed status values needs pricing, waiting on answers, declined, quoted, sent, and the fictional QR-1001 row from the guided demo. Includes a Copy CSV button so the person can start their own spreadsheet.

kit_contents.title: Reply Review Checklist
kit_contents.purpose: Interactive, session-only checklist used before contacting the requester. It confirms that every CONFIRMED fact appears in the request, that labels are separate, that fit used only the written rules, that unusual requests were not auto-rejected, that the draft has no price or internal notes, and that the person will price and send themselves.

kit_contents.title: Fictional Sample Requests
kit_contents.purpose: The same fictional Jordan Hale deck request used in the guided demo, plus a second fictional roofing request in Mesa labelled FIT NO, both labelled as fictional, with a Copy text button. The person can practice extraction and fit rules in their AI tool before using a real request.

kit_contents.title: Data and Safety Guidance
kit_contents.purpose: Rules for handling quote requests in AI tools: review data settings, remove payment details, do not paste passwords, do not put prices or internal cost notes in a draft, do not send the draft, and do not auto-reject an unusual request that might still be a good lead. It also states that file upload support differs by plan and that nothing is sent, edited, or paid automatically.

decision_rules: Apply the owner's written qualification rules before any FIT label. Do not judge fit from a generic 'sounds like a deck job' guess.
CONFIRMED fields may use only words the request stated. Do not invent square footage, budget, addresses, names, or dates.
Keep approximate wording. If the request says 'maybe 300 sq ft', the CONFIRMED size is 'maybe 300 sq ft', not 300.00.
If location is missing, write NEEDS YOUR CHECK. Do not assume the service area.
If size is missing, write NEEDS YOUR CHECK. Do not infer size from photos or from 'a regular backyard'.
If the work type is not in the offered list and is listed as out of scope, mark FIT NO and show the matching rule.
If the location is outside the written service area, mark FIT NO and show the matching rule.
If the work is close to the catalog but not listed (for example a curved custom deck when only deck replacement is offered), write NEEDS YOUR CHECK. Do not mark FIT NO.
A phrase such as 'if not crazy expensive' is AI INTERPRETATION about budget sensitivity, not a CONFIRMED budget.
A stated hope such as 'hoping before July' is a requested window, not a booked start date and not a confirmed deadline.
Never put prices, cost bands, markups, supplier names, or other internal notes in the draft acknowledgment.
The draft is a draft only. Do not send it. Do not create a CRM record or tracker row. Suggest the row; the person adds it.
Do not generate a price, a range, or a 'ballpark'. Pricing is the person's job after they review scope.
List every skipped or NO-fit request with its rule. Do not hide a rejected request.
On a later request, start from the new pasted text and the current written rules. Do not reuse a previous requester's size, location, or timeline.
human_ai_boundary: AI extracts stated fields and labels CONFIRMED separately from AI INTERPRETATION. The person decides whether a field was actually stated.
AI applies the qualification rules the owner wrote. The person writes those rules and decides whether an unusual request is still worth a quote.
AI writes FIT YES, FIT NO, or NEEDS YOUR CHECK with the matching rule. The person decides whether to quote, decline, or ask more.
AI lists clarifying questions and drafts an acknowledgment with no price. The person edits the questions and the draft, or discards them.
AI suggests a tracker row. The person adds, changes, or skips that row in their own sheet or CRM.
AI never sends email, never prices the job, never edits a CRM, and never uploads the person's request to a third party. The person prices and sends, or decides not to.
The person decides whether any recommended action happens.
safety: Nothing is sent, edited, cancelled, or paid automatically. Every page states that the person prices and sends, and that the kit changes nothing.
Atlas does not connect to a website form, inbox, CRM, sheet, or any other vendor. It has no OAuth flow, no API call, and does not upload the person's data to any third party.

Before pasting a request into an AI tool, the person is told to review that tool's data settings (such as chat history, training use, and file retention) and to remove payment details and other columns the workflow does not need.
The kit tells the person not to paste account passwords, payment card numbers, or bank details into the AI tool.
File upload support and data controls in ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini differ by plan, account, and admin settings. The kit says so and does not claim any plan includes a specific capability.
The kit tells the person not to put prices, cost bands, markups, or supplier names in a customer-facing draft, and not to send the draft from the kit.
The kit tells the person not to mark FIT NO on an unusual request that is close to the catalog. That case is NEEDS YOUR CHECK so a good lead is not dropped in silence.
All demo and sample data is fictional and labelled as fictional on the page.
Worksheet entries and checklist progress stay in the browser session only and are not saved to Atlas.
The pages contain no statistics, savings, ROI claims, prices, or checkout. Fictional sizes such as 300 sq ft and 150 sq ft are measurements, not dollar figures.
required_data_tools: The quote request as pasted form or email text
A written service catalog (what the shop offers)
Owner-written qualification rules (service area, minimum size, out-of-scope work, never-in-draft notes)
A sheet or CRM the person updates themselves
A file-capable AI assistant. File upload support differs by plan, account, and admin settings; the request can be pasted as text instead.
